title: Fourteen Autumns and One Short Desk
subtitle: 新闻出版 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 新闻出版（人与社会·文学艺术与体育）
meta: 主题语境：新闻出版（人与社会·文学艺术与体育）　|　核心词汇：editor　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 editor 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 my aunt ① met an editor that no writer in the office would have thanked, and she said the meeting was the whole of the autumn. The ② editor, meaning the person and not the program, ran fourteen autumns and stayed unnamed in the book; an editor, she said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left unthanked.

Every ③ editor in that office had the same short desk at the end of it, and the ④ editor at the end, meaning the one they kept for the night shift and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An editor, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to thank; my aunt said the thanking is the part that fills fourteen autumns.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the editor was the whole of the story, meaning the program and not the person. The ⑥ editor, meaning the program and not any of that, is the only thing in a story that everybody uses and nobody thanks; editor, he said, is either something you meet or the only word that means both a person and a program. He said the program is the part they remember.

By 1967 the ⑦ editor had become a line in a list, and the list had become an argument about the short desk. The ⑧ editor of the whole thing, my aunt wrote in October, was one office and fourteen autumns of thanking; editor, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to thank. She said the thanking was never mentioned.

The ⑨ editor I remember is the one named in the list, who retired in 1979 and is still described as the quietest in the office. An ⑩ editor, my mother said in 1981, is the only one who improves by being thanked; every editor, she said, is a program that has agreed to look like a person. She said the program was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 编辑；编者（指那间报馆里共事过的那一位）
B. n. 编辑；编者（指那位编辑本人，与编辑程序相对）
C. 固定搭配：meet an editor 见一位编辑
D. n. 编辑；编者（指留给夜班的那一位）
E. n. 编辑；编者（抽象总称，指一间报馆的编稿之事）
F. n. 编辑；编者（指名单上写到、被列名的那一位）
G. n. 编辑程序；剪辑器（指故事里人人都用却无人感谢的那样东西）
H. n. 编辑程序（抽象总称，指人人都用却无人感谢的那种工具）

items.q: met an editor that no writer in the office would have thanked
The editor, meaning the person and not the program
the editor was the whole of the story
the editor had become a line in a list
The editor of the whole thing
An editor, my mother said in 1981

answers.why: meet an editor 意为“见一位编辑”，1958 年姑姑见了一位报馆里没有一位作者肯道谢的编辑。
editor 意为“编辑、编者”，指那位编辑本人而不是编辑程序，他经过了十四个秋天而在簿子上没有名字。
editor 意为“编辑、编者”，指那间报馆里的每一位编辑，每一位到头都有同一张小小的办公桌。
editor 意为“编辑、编者”，指留给夜班的那一位，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
editor 意为“编辑程序、剪辑器”，指故事里人人都用却无人感谢的那样东西，叔叔说这个编辑程序就是那个故事的全部。
editor 意为“编辑程序”，指人人都用却无人感谢的那种工具而不是那位编辑，是故事里人人都用、却无人感谢的东西。
editor 意为“编辑、编者”，指名单上写到、被列名的那一位，到 1967 年这位编辑成了名单里的一行。
editor 意为“编辑、编者”，姑姑十月写道，整件事的编稿之事是一间报馆和十四个秋天的道谢。
editor 意为“编辑、编者”，我记得的是名单上列名的那一位，1979 年退休了，至今仍被说成报馆里最安静的一位。
editor 为抽象总称，母亲 1981 年说，一位编辑是唯一会因为被好好道谢而变得更好的人。
